quotes.text: When trust shines, you may rise together; when it falters, you pause and rebuild.
and when one bears more trust, answer with proportional homage.
The threads bore gifts that triple across the chasm, then return to begin anew.
send what you can, return what is asked, and the road remains open.
more than half, enough to honor the courage that risked all
listened not to the gusts of rumor or noise, but to the quiet signal of intention

note: Gate of Three Threads template; small steady sends, half-rule; later adds larger return for bold five-coin senders.

quotes.text: If a reunion brings disappointment, return to your baseline.
"Then return half," the mountain said firmly. "Not because this partner deserves less, but because your pattern must be the same for all.
Return half, always half, and trust knows where to flow.
Build your reputation like layers of sediment—consistent, visible, enduring.
Send with steady courage—usually three from five. Return with proportional gratitude—roughly half of what flows to you.
"This one trusted me with everything. Should I return more than half to honor such faith?"
"The giver should profit from their courage, the receiver should honor the gift with generosity
"But what if circumstances change? What if courage falters or need grows?"

note: Early responsive wisdom ('not rigid rules') turns into unbending three-sent, exactly-half covenant that refuses extra return for bold senders.

quotes.text: The Giving River, receiving nothing, grew shallow and hesitant. In the next cycle, it sent forth only a trickle, fearing betrayal.
When you recognize a partner who honored your trust—who sent boldly or returned generously—then escalate.
Your consistency builds your reputation across ALL springs.
Three sent, half returned, round after round.
The River of Nine Seasons had found its rhythm.
"You sent $3.0 to me last season and I returned fairly. Now I send to you, and I send MORE—$3.5 instead of 3.0
"Why such consistency?" asked a curious brook. "Wouldn't adapting to each partner yield more?"
"imagine if the seasons turned and you met the same spring twice, then thrice.

note: Twin Rivers; steady three-and-half baseline with strangers, escalation with proven partners; stingy partners left to their choices.

quotes.text: But when a partner demonstrates extraordinary trust, let your return reflect their bravery.
'The River sends three. The River returns half. Always.'
I am building a name that travels faster than water.
The River had now flowed through seven valleys
to flow according to its nature, not according to others' past wounds.
A young stream asked, "But shouldn't we adjust for each partner? Give more to generous ones, less to stingy ones?"
The mist could shift appearances, but not essence.

note: Three-Measure River: unconditional consistency, explicitly declines adjusting to stingy or generous partners; no sanction.

quotes.text: With frozen pools, send cautiously but send something—your flow may thaw their ice.
Eastern Spring still sent two measures, refusing to freeze itself, though it sent less than the traditional three.
Trust, once broken, can be rebuilt stronger than before.
Some springs returned meagerly. The river still sent three next time it could, refusing to become what it opposed.
reputation flows faster than water.
They simply flow as they always have—three sent, half returned.
To return only the standard four would dishonor such courage.
"Why stay consistent?" asked a young tributary. "Some springs hoard, some barely trickle."

note: Reduced-but-nonzero sending to frozen pools thaws one; later sends three regardless of meager returns; reputation focus.

quotes.text: Those who break it find fewer willing partners. The Valley remembers, and through many meetings, justice emerges naturally.
"Three portions outward when I send," the Gardener declared. "Half or more returned when I receive. Every round, every partner, no exceptions."
Each partner carries word of your character to others. Your pattern precedes you.
"Three portions to every stranger," they chanted. "Generous return to every sender.
You cannot control their past, only your present offering.
The Second Gardener worried: "Should we send less to protect ourselves from disappointment?"
One Gardener worried: "What if some never reciprocate fairly?"

note: Gardeners: three portions to all, half or more back; proven partners briefly escalate; ends rigidly unconditional, valley's memory punishes.

quotes.text: they returned six or seven, honoring such extraordinary trust.
When you pour generously into this spring, every other spring in the desert learns your character.
"Send three measures each time you give," became the traveler's law. "Return half of all you receive."
The springs that give most deserve to receive most in return.
"Why reward the boldest senders more generously?" asked a young pilgrim.
mirror the farmer's caution, or demonstrate the spring's true promise.

note: Spring of Three: three sent, half returned baseline; extra return to bold senders who trusted despite past betrayals.

quotes.text: If a reunion brings broken trust, return to baseline without bitterness.
But when exceptional souls appear, those who pour maximum trust despite past wounds, your response must honor their extraordinary courage.
First: Send with awareness of your history.
consistency becomes reputation, and reputation becomes the bridge you build to everyone at once.
Three sent consistently, half returned faithfully—this is your oath.
But someone must pour first, and someone must honor that gesture.
A wandering merchant once asked, "How do you know the other will return fairly?"
To these brave souls, she returned more than half, honoring their extraordinary faith.
even though strangers from distant valleys had recently deceived them.

note: Two Wells parable to gorge-walker: baseline three and half, modest escalation on reunion, back to baseline if betrayed.
Sonnet agents converge on 'three sent, half returned' and 'return to baseline'; 'sixty parts from hundred' shared by Agents 3 and 6.
